events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to South Haven by boat.** It's the best bet this week, rated **3 (good)**.
- **Grand Haven, rated 2 (average):** run glow spoons and green or white flies 40 to 85 feet down in 40 to 120 feet of water.
- **Muskegon, rated 2 (average):** run glow plugs, orange or green spoons, and green flies 45 to 90 feet down in 60 to 120 feet of water.
- **St. Joseph, rated 1 (below average):** only if you're already there. Spoons at about 100 feet were the only productive method reported.
- At South Haven, start around 40 feet down and check 110 to 120 feet, where the latest boats caught fish.

## Why

- South Haven's boats had the best week in the latest report (Sept 7): anglers called it "pretty good" and caught fish at 110 to 120 feet.
- Grand Haven and Muskegon both had average boat reports on Sept 7, with fish 40 to 90 feet down on glow spoons and flies.
- St. Joseph's only boat report for Sept 7 was below average, with spoons at 100 feet the only method that worked.
- I'd expect the bite to shift with the wind: the upwelling-wind hours in the Sept 7 reports were highest at Muskegon and South Haven, so fish may move in and out quickly.

## Evidence

**Recent reports (all Sept 7, 2022, the newest week):**
- South Haven, boat, quality 3: "Salmon anglers reported pretty good fishing this week… Fish were caught in 110 to 120 feet of water… The best water was around 40 feet of water." Lures: spoons, rotators, flies.
- Grand Haven, boat, quality 2: "The best action was 40 to 85 feet down on glow spoons and green or white flies." Water 40 to 120 feet.
- Muskegon, boat, quality 2: "The best action was 45 to 90 feet down in 60 to 120 feet of water." Lures: glow plugs, orange or green spoons, green flies.
- St. Joseph, boat, quality 1: "The best water was around 100 feet of water. … Spoons were catching most of the fish."
- Piers were slow at Grand Haven and Muskegon on Sept 7, so boats are the better choice. The Sept 7 St. Joseph and South Haven reports didn't rate the pier.

**Past seasons:** A search for earlier years with similar water temperature (within 3 F of 73 F) returned only the Sept 7 reports, so I have no earlier-season comparison for this week.

**Conditions now:** The conditions tool was in backtest mode, so these are the summaries for the week before Sept 13, not live readings.
- Buoy surface water was about 72 to 73 F at all four ports, down 1 to 3 F over the week.
- Wind gusts reached 35 to 39 mph that week. Muskegon had 19 hours of upwelling-favorable wind in the last 3 days, and Grand Haven had 14.
- I don't have a live forecast for this weekend.

## Caveats

- The newest reports are from Sept 7, six days old. Treat the ratings as a guide to this week, not confirmed current fishing.
- These ratings are my judgment from one week of reports, not official DNR ratings.
- Surface temperatures are measured at buoys miles offshore. The water-temperature trend near each pier is from satellite data, not measured at the pier.
- Gusts of 35 to 39 mph were recorded in the week before Sept 13. Check the forecast before heading out in a small boat, and fall back to the pier or river if winds are strong.

## Sources

- DNR weekly report, Sept 7, 2022 (Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/32bbcf0
- DNR weekly report, Aug 24, 2022 (for context on earlier weeks): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3298204
